methods_measured.span: Crystal structure and vibrational characteristics were characterized using an X-ray diffractometer (XRD; PANalytical X’Pert Pro MPD), a Fourier transform infrared spectrometer (FTIR; Bruker Inventio-S), and a Raman spectrometer (Horiba T64000).
a Fourier transform infrared spectrometer (FTIR; Bruker Inventio-S)
Bulk densities were measured using the Archimedes method.
Surface morphologies were examined using a scanning electron microscope (SEM; JEOL JSM5910LV).

A transmission electron microscope (TEM; JEOL JEM-2100Plus) operated at $2 0 0 ~ \mathrm { k V }$ was employed to investigate local microstructures, and selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns were obtained to analyze local structural features.

Surface chemical states were characterized using an X-ray photoelectron spectrometer (XPS; ULVAC-PHI VersaProbe 4), with binding energies calibrated against the C 1s peak at $2 8 4 . 8 \ : \mathrm { e V } .$

methods_measured.quantity: dielectric constant and loss vs T and f
methods_measured.span: Temperatureand frequency-dependent dielectric properties (30–500 ${ } ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } ,$ 1 kHz–1 MHz) were measured using an LCR meter (Agilent Technologies).

Polarization–electric field $\left( P \mathrm { - } E \right)$ hysteresis loops were recorded with a ferroelectric tester (Radiant Technologies, Radiant Precision; $1 0 \mathrm { k V } ,$ ) under an applied field of $6 0 \ \mathrm { k V / c m }$ at $0 . 1 \ \mathrm { H z }$ and RT.

methods_measured.instrument: MTI Instruments, MTI-2100 optical displacement sensor
methods_measured.span: Strain–electric field (S–E) responses were evaluated at RT using an optical displacement sensor (MTI Instruments, MTI-2100) under the same measurement conditions as those used for the $P { - } E$ measurements.

mechanisms.mechanism: Zr-induced lattice softening + R3c–P4bm phase coexistence flattening free-energy landscape -> reversible electrostriction-dominated strain
mechanisms.span: The enhanced electromechanical response originates from $Z \boldsymbol { \mathsf { r } }$ -induced lattice softening and R3c–P4bm phase coexistence, which flatten the free-energy landscape and promote reversible field-driven polarization dynamics.

mechanisms.mechanism: suppression of irreversible domain-wall motion via reduced Pr and Ec
mechanisms.span: The reduced remanent polarization and coercive field suppress irreversible domain-wall motion, thereby favoring electrostriction-governed strain generation.

mechanisms.mechanism: transition from non-ergodic ferroelectric to ergodic relaxor state with Zr

mechanisms.mechanism: grain growth controlled solely by lattice distortion
mechanisms.span: Therefore, the grain-growth behavior cannot be attributed solely to lattice distortion and is likely influenced by multiple factors during sintering [18,20−22].

mechanisms.mechanism: XPS as proof of bulk oxygen-vacancy concentration
mechanisms.span: These observations further suggest that the XPS results presented herein should be interpreted primarily as evidence of near-surface electronic and chemical modifications rather than as direct proof of bulk oxygen vacancy concentration.

summary: CC BY 4.0 JAC article on Zr-substituted BNKT piezoceramics with a clean 4-member composition series (x = 0.000, 0.005, 0.015, 0.025) measured with SEM, XRD/Rietveld, Raman, FTIR, LCR dielectric, P–E and S–E on the same compositions; TEM and XPS only on x = 0.000 and 0.015. Mechanism: lattice softening + R3c–P4bm coexistence -> electrostriction-dominated strain; antiferroelectric phase explicitly rejected.
